explanation_es:
El present perfect conecta el pasado con el presente. Se forma con have o has más el participio pasado del verbo. Con I, you, we y they se usa have; con he, she e it se usa has. En los verbos regulares el participio termina en -ed (worked, studied); en los irregulares es la tercera columna y hay que aprenderla (done, been, gone, seen, written).

Afirmativa: I have finished the module. Negativa: I haven't finished the module. Pregunta: Have you finished the module? Respuesta corta: Yes, I have / No, I haven't. Al hablar casi siempre se contrae: I've, you've, he's.

Se usa en tres casos. Uno: experiencias sin decir cuándo (I have worked with databases). Dos: algo que empezó en el pasado y todavía sigue (I have studied at SENA since 2024). Tres: acciones recientes con resultado ahora (I have just sent the report).

Se parece al español "he hecho", pero hay una diferencia clave: en inglés el present perfect nunca va con un tiempo terminado. Si la frase tiene yesterday, last week, ago o una fecha, va en past simple: I finished the project yesterday. En cambio, si el periodo no ha terminado (today, this week, this year) o no importa cuándo pasó, normalmente va en present perfect, aunque en Colombia digamos "esta semana aprendí mucho" o "¿alguna vez usaste...?" con pretérito.

Palabras señal: ever y never (experiencias); just, already y yet (acciones recientes). Just y already van entre have y el participio; yet va al final en negativas y preguntas. Since va con un punto de inicio (since 2020) y for con una duración (for five years). "Hace cinco años que trabajo aquí" es I have worked here for five years, nunca "since five years". Cuidado con been y gone: she has been to Bogotá significa que estuvo allá y ya volvió; she has gone to Bogotá, que se fue y todavía está allá.

contrast.en: I have worked on three projects at SENA.
contrast.es: He trabajado en tres proyectos en el SENA.
contrast.note_es: Experiencia sin fecha: importa que ya pasó, no cuándo. Por eso va en present perfect.

contrast.en: I worked on a project last year.
contrast.es: Trabajé en un proyecto el año pasado.
contrast.note_es: Last year es un tiempo terminado, así que va en past simple. Nunca digas 'I have worked last year'.

contrast.en: I have studied programming for two years.
contrast.note_es: En español decimos 'llevo dos años' o 'hace dos años que estudio'; en inglés es present perfect con for más la duración.

contrast.en: I have been in the ADSO program since 2024.
contrast.es: Estoy en el programa ADSO desde 2024.
contrast.note_es: Since marca el punto de inicio. En español va en presente ('estoy'), en inglés en present perfect: decir 'I am in the program since 2024' es un error.

En Colombia también decimos '¿alguna vez usaste...?' con pretérito, pero en inglés una experiencia sin fecha va en present perfect. Ever va entre el sujeto y el participio. Para responder que no: No, I have never used it.

contrast.en: I haven't finished the database yet.
contrast.es: Todavía no he terminado la base de datos.
contrast.note_es: Yet va al final de la frase; en español 'todavía' puede ir al principio. Con este sentido, yet se usa en negativas y preguntas; en afirmativas se usa already.

contrast.en: My instructor has gone to Medellín.
contrast.es: Mi instructor se fue para Medellín.
contrast.note_es: Gone indica que se fue y todavía no ha vuelto. Si ya estuvo allá y regresó, se dice: My instructor has been to Medellín.

common_errors.wrong: I have finished the project yesterday.
common_errors.why_es: Yesterday es un tiempo terminado. Con yesterday, last week, ago o una fecha exacta se usa past simple, aunque el resultado se note ahora. El present perfect nunca va con un tiempo cerrado.

common_errors.wrong: I have worked here since three years.
common_errors.right: I have worked here for three years.
common_errors.why_es: Since es para un punto de inicio (since 2023, since Monday) y for es para una duración (for three years). El error viene de traducir 'desde hace tres años' con since.

common_errors.wrong: I have never saw that error.
common_errors.right: I have never seen that error.
common_errors.why_es: Después de have o has va el participio pasado, no el past simple. En los irregulares es la tercera columna: see, saw, seen; go, went, gone; do, did, done.
Con he, she e it el auxiliar es has. Es parecido al error de olvidar la -s de la tercera persona en presente simple.

common_errors.wrong: I don't have finished the report.
common_errors.why_es: La negación va en el mismo auxiliar: haven't o hasn't. Don't y doesn't son del presente simple, no del present perfect.

common_errors.wrong: I haven't finished yet the report.
common_errors.right: I haven't finished the report yet.
common_errors.why_es: Yet va al final de la frase, después del complemento. El error viene de copiar el orden del español 'no he terminado todavía el informe'.

common_errors.wrong: I study English for three years.
common_errors.right: I have studied English for three years.
common_errors.why_es: Para algo que empezó en el pasado y sigue ahora no se usa presente simple. 'Hace tres años que estudio inglés' o 'llevo tres años estudiando inglés' se dice con present perfect y for.

oral_questions.question: Have you ever worked for a company?
oral_questions.model_answer: No, I haven't. I have never worked for a company, but I have done a project for the agribusiness center at SENA.
oral_questions.focus: Have you ever + participio; respuesta corta y never

oral_questions.question: How long have you studied English?
oral_questions.model_answer: I have studied English for about two years. I started my course at SENA in 2024.
oral_questions.focus: How long + present perfect con for; past simple para el momento de inicio

oral_questions.question: What have you learned this year?
oral_questions.model_answer: This year I have learned SQL and I have built a database for my project. I have also improved my English.
oral_questions.focus: Tiempo no terminado (this year) con present perfect

oral_questions.question: Have you finished the project yet?
oral_questions.model_answer: Not yet. We have finished the login page and the database, but we haven't finished the reports module yet.
oral_questions.focus: Yet al final en pregunta y negativa

oral_questions.question: How many programming languages have you used?
oral_questions.model_answer: I have used Python, JavaScript and PHP. I have just started learning Java.
oral_questions.focus: How many + present perfect; just para acción reciente

oral_questions.question: Which cities in Colombia have you been to?
oral_questions.model_answer: I have been to Bogotá and Medellín. I haven't been to Cartagena yet, but I would like to go.
oral_questions.focus: Been to para lugares visitados; haven't ... yet

oral_questions.question: Who has helped you with your project?
oral_questions.model_answer: My instructor has helped me a lot with the database design. A classmate has also helped me with the tests.
oral_questions.focus: Has con tercera persona (my instructor, a classmate)

oral_questions.question: Has your team presented the project yet?
oral_questions.model_answer: No, we haven't presented it yet because we haven't finished the reports module. We have already finished the user registration form.
oral_questions.focus: Negativa con haven't ... yet y already en afirmativa

oral_questions.question: What has changed in your life since you started at SENA?
oral_questions.model_answer: Since I started at SENA, I have learned how to program and I have made new friends. I have also become more organized.
oral_questions.focus: Since + past simple en la frase de tiempo, present perfect en la principal

oral_questions.question: Has your project ever failed a test?
oral_questions.model_answer: Yes, it has. The login page has failed a few times, but we have already fixed the problem.
oral_questions.focus: Has + it; respuesta corta Yes, it has; already

roleplay.situation_es: Tu instructor del SENA pasa por tu mesa a revisar cómo va el proyecto de control de acceso para el centro agroempresarial. Te pregunta qué han hecho, qué falta y qué has aprendido. Fíjate en que respondes con present perfect cuando no hay fecha y cambias a past simple cuando das un momento exacto (last Friday, in June).

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.line: Good morning. How is the access control project going? What have you done so far?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: Good morning. We have finished the database and the login module. We have also created the staff registration form.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.line: Great. Have you tested the login module yet?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: Yes, we have. We tested it last Friday and found two bugs, but we have already fixed them.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.line: Good. What about the warehouse module? Has your team started it?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: We have started it, but we haven't finished it yet. We have only done the item list.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.line: How long have you worked on this project?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: We have worked on it for three months. We started in June.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.line: Have you ever used a web framework before?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: No, I haven't. This is the first time I have used one, and I have learned a lot since we started.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.line: Excellent. Where is your teammate today?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: He has gone to the warehouse to take photos of the equipment. He hasn't come back yet.
